topic: Introduction to Topology: The Geometry of Rubber Sheets

sections.title: The Hook: Geometry vs. Topology
lecture_lines: Geometry focuses on rigid shapes and fixed measurements.
Topology studies shapes under smooth, continuous deformation.
We can stretch, bend, or twist objects.
But we cannot tear or glue them.
A square and circle are topologically identical.
animations: Display two distinct geometric shapes on screen, represented by [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/coffee.svg] and [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/donut.svg].
Apply continuous stretching and bending to both shapes.
Show shapes becoming identical via continuous deformation, transforming into a unified [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/mug.svg].

sections.title: Core Concept: Homeomorphism
lecture_lines: Homeomorphism is a continuous, reversible transformation.
Think: no tearing and no gluing allowed.
Holes serve as a shape's fundamental fingerprint.
animations: Show two mugs, one small [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/mug.svg] and one large [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/mug.svg].
Demonstrate stretching the small [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/mug.svg] into the large [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/mug.svg] one.
Highlight preservation of one handle hole on the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/mug.svg].

sections.title: The Genus: Counting Holes
lecture_lines: Genus counts the holes in a surface.
A sphere has zero holes, so genus zero.
You cannot change genus without cutting.
animations: Introduce a sphere [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sphere.svg], a torus [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/torus.svg], and a double-torus.
Count the holes in each shape clearly.
Label sphere [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sphere.svg] G=0, torus [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/torus.svg] G=1, double-torus G=2.

sections.title: Real-World Application: The Map Coloring Problem
lecture_lines: Topology ignores distance to focus on connections.
Complex maps simplify into essential network graphs.
Connections remain the same despite physical distortion.
animations: Show a flat 2D map with several regions using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/map.svg].
Fill regions with four distinct colors such that neighbors differ.
Explain this works for any map on a sphere using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sphere.svg].

sections.title: Conclusion: Beyond Surfaces
lecture_lines: Topology captures the global properties of objects.
It ignores local measurements like size or angle.
Advanced topics like knots offer deeper insights.
animations: Summarize the key concepts of topology using a [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/mug.svg] to illustrate continuous deformation.
Transition to viewing objects by their global connectivity.
Display a closing screen with encouragement and a [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/donut.svg].
